Harden `accounts_public_base_url` against a poisoned `x-forwarded-proto` header. Modal's ingress passes that client-supplied header through unsanitized, and its value was spliced verbatim into the derived base URL, so a crafted proto (e.g. `https://evil.example/?`) could change the constructed URL's effective host on tiers without a configured `ACCOUNTS_BASE_URL` (dev/CI). The header is now trusted only when it is exactly `http` or `https`; any other value falls back to the ASGI request scheme. Production and staging were never affected (they set `ACCOUNTS_BASE_URL`, which wins), and the OAuth callback path was already backstopped by the redirector's host allowlist -- this closes the injection at the source as defense-in-depth.
